rationale: wu_2015-claude-agentic: wu_n_bands=6, wu_n_outer=4, wu_motion_range=8, wu_motion_window=2, wu_soft_thresh=0.0015, val_n=200, val_chunk=4, seed=42, rationale=ITER-4 (one knob vs iter-1). NUMBERS: iter-2 (n_bands6,n_outer0) RMSE=0.401; iter-3 (n_bands1,n_outer0) RMSE=0.231. NPZ ANALYSIS of iter-3: the aliasing_free_fbp step-1 output is ~205x too small (pred mean 1.05e-4 vs plain-FBP baseline 0.068) and only 0.44-correlated with baseline -> aliasing_free_fbp omits the FBP normalisation constant AND the radial band-weighting decorrelates structure. So step-1 alone can NEVER reach baseline. But iter-1 (n_bands6,n_outer2) reached RMSE=0.0247 -- the OUTER residual-refinement loop (forward-project, residual, densify, FBP add-back) is what pulls the recon back toward the measured data each pass, progressively correcting the step-1 scale/structure error. ONE KNOB: wu_n_outer 2 -> 4 (n_bands back to 6 = iter-1 base). HYPOTHESIS: if more residual add-back passes keep reducing RMSE monotonically (each pass re-injects the measured-minus-forward residual, a data-consistency correction), 4 passes should push RMSE below iter-1s 0.0247 toward the 0.00521 baseline and possibly clear hr>0; if RMSE plateaus/rises, the residual densification noise cancels the correction and n_outer has an interior optimum. Budget: 4 passes ~ 2x iter-1 recon, still seconds, <20min.
